excerpts: Any disk or data source connected to your Mac and recognized by macOS as a file system can be scanned with DaisyDisk
No automated cleaning is performed
The user makes the informed decision which files are no longer needed and can be deleted.
Built-in QuickLook allows you to instantly preview files of any type

sources.title: Deleting files
excerpts: Don’t worry, the files remain intact until you click the Delete button.
Clicking the Delete button starts deletion process, but you’ll have 5 seconds to change your mind and press Cancel.
DaisyDisk permanently removes files and folders instead of moving them to the system Trash
So, when you delete a file, its copy may still be retained in the local snapshots, and still consume the same amount of disk space.

article.title: Read a DaisyDisk map without treating every large file as disposable
article.primaryIntent: Interpret a sunburst selection and decide whether to stage, keep, back up or remove a file, understanding permanent deletion and delayed free-space changes.
outline: Lead with deliberate selection, not promised savings; official app UI immediately after lead once cleared
Interpret petal size and drill down; size is not permission
Check ownership, backup and rebuild/download cost before staging
Review Collector and understand permanent deletion versus Trash
Explain snapshot caveat as vendor documentation, not measured results
One disclosed Breathing Room comparison for recurring investigation, with preview/hosted/runtime limits
article.interactionPass: Static decision checklist: recognize file? own it? backed up? rebuild cost acceptable? If any answer is unknown, keep and investigate. No deletion button, filesystem access or fabricated calculation.
article.length: Earned, normally 900–1800 words; no padding, forced FAQ, code demo or invented search-volume evidence.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs DaisyDisk: disk maps or ongoing investigation
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose a documented Mac storage workflow, not declare a universal winner.
rows: D6/B3 deletion methods and approval exceptions

daisydiskAdvantages: Documented proportional sunburst navigation and Quick Look support suit manual visual triage (D5).
One-time displayed price and personal multi-Mac licence avoid recurring purchase payments for that licence; major upgrades are qualified (D3).
Current advertised minimum macOS is older than Breathing Room’s (D2/B2); not a compatibility benchmark.
daisydiskTradeoffs: Permanent deletion is materially different from Trash movement (D6).
App Store and stand-alone advanced features differ (D8).
Trial needs email and some features remain restricted (D4).
breathingRoomFit: Consider the preview’s source-implemented grouped processes/activity and exact saved-approval workflow when the job extends beyond a one-off map (B3); do not claim DaisyDisk lacks those features.
Free local core differs from optional paid hosted AI Care (B1), with installation and native-validation caveats (B2).
notClaims: No speed, savings, safety superiority, hands-on experience or unsupported competitor absence claims.
